description: Psa 89:5-7 Heavens— the heavenly realm itself, the location of the assembly. Assembly of the saints (qahal qedoshim) — the gathered company of holy beings who stand around Yahweh. “Saints” here is not human believers; the parallel in verse 6 with “sons of the mighty” and the setting “in the heavens” mark them as members of the divine council. Sons of the mighty (bene elim) — the same class of lesser divine beings. Elim is the plural of El (god or mighty one - never mankind); the phrase identifies them as gods / sons of God under Yahweh, not as human rulers. The three terms describe one scene: 1. Yahweh is incomparable among the heavenly beings who form his council. 2. No member of that assembly is his equal. 3. The passage places the divine court in the heavens and distinguishes its members from Yahweh himself.
